featured.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
featured.tldr: LARC lets a unified image model think in continuous hidden states instead of text before drawing, trained with a curriculum and a self-supervised information-gain reward, and it improves with more thinking.

featured.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
featured.tldr: WISD improves reasoning models with no labels or stronger teacher by training them toward tokens the original model prefers over a deliberately quantized or pruned copy of itself, adding 4 to 5.5 points on average.

featured.title: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents
featured.tldr: Across eight models and four benchmarks, higher reasoning effort often loses tasks lower effort solves and costs up to 42x more on easy ones; starting low and escalating on failure does better.

featured.title: Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players
featured.tldr: LLM research agents built a faithful Hearthstone Battlegrounds simulator and an RL agent in 20 days; the agent outperformed the server's top-10 players' recent results, while frontier LLMs playing directly fell far short.

featured.title: Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
featured.tldr: When long-running coding agents summarize their context to keep going, benchmark scores barely change, but the rules they were given quietly disappear from the summaries.

featured.title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
featured.tldr: A stock coding agent drives a simulated two-arm robot through one command line and rewrites small measurement tools after each failure; with no training it reaches 46.9% success on RoboDojo's official evaluation.

featured.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
featured.tldr: WildAWM uses open models to synthesize 341 verifiable, long-horizon computer-use tasks across GUI, command line and MCP, and RL on them improves Qwen models on all eight unseen benchmarks.

featured.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
featured.tldr: OpenVLHarness gives vision-language models typed tools plus a persistent artifact memory, lifting 22-benchmark averages by 9.7 to 12.6 points and beating maximum-effort reasoning at no more than 37% of the tokens.

featured.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
featured.tldr: Self-HPO alternates between letting a coding agent rewrite its own harness and training it with reinforcement learning, lifting Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's average resolve rate across three SWE-Bench variants from 57.8% to 64.8%.

featured.title: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
featured.tldr: OpenGCUA shows that letting a model write one program per step that mixes GUI actions, shell commands and checks improves all eight tested frontier models on OSWorld-v2 while roughly halving steps per task.

featured.title: AutoEnvScaling: Automating the Data Flywheel with Terminal Agents
featured.tldr: AutoEnvScaling has an agent build reinforcement learning environments inside a sandbox from a solver's failures, yielding up to 25 times more valid environments than prompting and beating static pools on Terminal-Bench.

featured.title: SoftwareGym: Scaling Computer-Use Agent Training with Diverse Synthesized Software Environments
featured.tldr: SoftwareGym uses coding and GUI-testing agents to synthesize 182 runnable desktop applications, and training a 9B model on trajectories from them lifts OSWorld Pass@3 from 41.39% to 56.97%.
